name: coordinate-agents
description: Coordinate multiple AI coding agents through a local-first, recoverable Agent Bus.

paragraphs: Coordinate Agents is a local Web Workspace for Codex + Antigravity collaboration. npm 3.0.1 is the Web-first distribution: a small standalone workbench with paired terminals, project/task persistence and lightweight role prompts.

Node 18 retains the owned stdio fallback. On Windows Node >=20, npm 3.0.1 verifies native PTY startup and real TTY behavior in a disposable, detached Session Host before selecting node-pty. A failed or timed-out probe selects stdio fallback only after owned-process cleanup is confirmed; an actual Session failure never automatically retries an Agent task. Session diagnostics include backend. Fallback preserves bounded I/O/lifecycle, but is not a real terminal and cannot provide native TUI or child-observed resize.

The GitHub Plugin / Legacy CLI / MCP / Task Graph source remains complete, including its local-first coordination protocol and runtime. Install the GitHub Plugin for structured collaboration; its version is managed independently (currently 2.4.0). npm 3.x excludes Plugin manifests, Skill resources, MCP, Task Graph, Adapter SDK/conformance/examples, tests and developer tooling. Only required runtime modules and the trusted notification script remain under skills/ in the tarball; this is not a packaged Codex Skill. No build or prepack step is needed.
features: Codex clarifies the task, records acceptance criteria, dispatches work, and reviews evidence.
A configured Implementer CLI edits code and runs tests inside an owned execution session.
The Agent Bus preserves task, message, review, session, and recovery facts locally.
Release actions stay separate from implementation and require explicit user authorization.

whatItDoes.text: Coordinate Agents is a local Web Workspace for Codex + Antigravity collaboration. npm 3.0.1 is the Web-first distribution: a small standalone workbench with paired terminals, project/task persistence and lightweight role prompts.

requirements.text: Install Node.js >=18, Git, and the Codex/Antigravity CLIs separately; sign in to each CLI before starting a task.
Focused behavior changes should include isolated tests and must not invoke live model accounts or modify a user's real project.
